ety.text: 1560s, via Middle French race from Italian razza (early 14th century), of uncertain origin. Partially displaced native Middle English kinde (“kind, type, sort, race, nature”), whence English kind. Fully displaced native Old English cnōsl and hād. theories * Diez and some other scholars suggest derivation from Proto-Germanic *raitō (whence Old High German reiza (“line”) and Old Norse ríta (“to score, log, outline”)), perhaps via Lombardic *raiza (“line”), which Körting notes is a literal rendering of Latin linea sanguinis (“bloodline of descent”).
Mid 16th century. From Middle French raïz, raiz, rais (“root”), from Latin radix (“root”), from Proto-Italic *wrādīks, from Proto-Indo-European *wréh₂ds.

A variant of raze. senses.d: A contest between people, animals, vehicles, etc. where the goal is to be the first to reach some objective.
ex: Several horses ran in a horse race: the first one to reach the finishing post won.
The race to cure cancer

senses.d: Swift progress; rapid motion; an instance of moving or driving at high speed.
ex: The flight of many birds is swifter than the race of any beasts.
Hence the rapid race / Of light, and lustre from th' effusive sun

senses.d: A race condition; a bug or problem that occurs when two or more components attempt to use the same resource at the same time.
ex: Many problems of oscillations and races are solved by this arrangement.

senses.d: A sequence of events; a progressive movement toward a goal.
ex: A race of wicked acts / Shall flow out of my anger, and o’erspread / The world’s wide face[.]

senses.d: A fast-moving current of water.
ex: Here are in these seas two dangerous races, the one called St. Alban's, the other Portland Race.

senses.d: A groove on a sewing machine or a loom along which the shuttle moves.

senses.d: A keno gambling session.

ex: The drivers were racing around the track.
"I cannot wait to race in front of the amazing home crowd," she added.

senses.d: To compete against in a race (contest).
ex: I raced him to the car, but he was there first, so he got to ride shotgun.

senses.d: To move or drive at high speed; to hurry or speed.
ex: As soon as it was time to go home, he raced for the door.
Her heart was racing as she peered into the dimly lit room.

senses.d: To run rapidly when not engaged to a transmission.
ex: "My mind is like a racing engine, tearing itself to pieces because it is not connected up with the work for which it was built."

senses.d: A large group of people distinguished from others on the basis of a common heritage.
ex: The Canadian race is one of the most vigorous on the globe.

senses.d: A large group of people distinguished from others on the basis of common physical characteristics, such as skin color or hair type.
ex: Race was a significant issue during apartheid in South Africa.

senses.d: A large group of people distinguished from others on the basis of shared characteristics or qualities, for example social qualities.
ex: The advent of the Internet has brought about a new race of entrepreneur.

senses.d: A large group of nonhumans distinguished from others on the basis of a common heritage.
ex: A treaty was concluded between the race of elves and the race of men.

A strain of plant with characteristics causing it to differ from other plants of the same species.
A breed or strain of domesticated animal.
ex: For do but note a wild and wanton herd, / Or race of youthful and unhandled colts, / Fetching mad bounds.

senses.d: A strain of microorganism, fungi, etc.
A category or kind of thing distinguished by common characteristics.
